entries.rationale: Isolated fake tools cover idempotent PATH normalization, virtualenv and shim-location precedence, shell and env-shebang dispatch, argv/cwd/status preservation, missing-helper/shim refusals and scoped missing-tool safeguards. Synthetic OpenCode-only credential fixtures cover per-launch key refresh, missing/empty-key precedence, fixed user paths, invalid-source refusals, isolated unrelated exports, suppressed source output and tracing, and shell-option restoration. Startup sentinels cover no mise/profile invocation; generic and Claude launches do not load OpenCode credentials, and containers and dry-run retain their host-helper-independent behavior. Live mise dispatch, credential validity and AoE rollout require separate verification.

behavior_requirements.description: Name a Beads close-policy or assignee refusal after landing, keep the tracking state, exit non-zero, and never pass --force.
Require the selected commit wrapper before preparing a merge; leave ordinary failures pending, reject false wrapper success and abort safely on an approved main update.
Reject unsafe merge or recovery state, fail closed for configured CI errors, and stop before feature merge when an approved main update changes the provider or evidence contract.

Pin exact SHAs, preserve Beads and cleanup ownership, never push main or tags, perform no CI or remote ref mutations in local-only mode, and persist GitHub landing receipts before real-success lease cleanup.
Validate selected file or note claims before and after landing, reject ambiguous, symlinked, or changed tracking, verify close readback, and retain note history or replaced state files.
Preserve fast-forward feature commits and actor-specific no-ff messages and identities without adding OpenCode attribution to Claude commits.
An approved --update-main either completes the feature merge or restores main to its pre-update SHA, and refuses to move main at all when the advertised ref carries no merge helper.
Route no-ff merges through real actor wrappers for one OpenCode GitHub bot co-author, rich or degraded agent trailers, actor identity, and preserved message paragraphs.

Advertise repository-specific capabilities, merge standalone with best-effort fetch in local-only mode, and support guarded batch landing with explicit exact-main CI preparation and independent cleanup outcomes.

entries.rationale: Existing integration coverage is retained as the first canonical suite.

behavior_requirements.description: Block task syntax failures and unavailable validators in normal and strict modes.

Keep managed-target validation dry-run only and avoid applying repository or host changes.
Wrap ansible/tasks YAML for local and container syntax checks on both entrypoints while checking playbooks directly and linting original inputs.
Dispatch managed, repository-only, template, shell, PowerShell, and config checks consistently.

behavior_requirements.description: Block pin drift, malformed release data, API failures, and hazardous successor notes.
Fail a Beads bump whose clone-local FK list differs from beads-sync's, and fail closed when bd's list cannot be fetched or parsed.
Reject redirects, pagination, and contents URLs outside the trusted Beads GitHub API before sending credentials.
Accept matching pins when no newer release exists or every successor is clean.

entries.rationale: The registered suite covers pin validation, SemVer ordering, release hazards, and trusted API boundaries.

behavior_requirements.description: Propagate pull, push, server, and remote failures without claiming synchronization succeeded.

Re-link the clone-local foreign keys dolt drops on reset and merge after pull, init, and conflict aborts, deleting orphans first, repair them on clean, report them in status (including a scan that cannot run), and keep both scripts' key lists identical.
Reject unsafe remotes and native-Windows peer operations before contacting or mutating Beads state.
Refuse a top-level bd sync before any native call while passing bd sync --help through, and set BD_NO_REMOTE_ADOPT on every native call the interactive wrappers make.
Dispatch supported shell and launcher operations to the intended guarded command.

entries.rationale: Registered helper and isolated sync suites cover launcher dispatch, platform and remote guards, dirty-state refusal, one-session pull SQL, snapshot boundaries, lifecycle cleanup, failure propagation, and URL redaction.
A registered offline suite covers manifest and path contracts, deterministic check/write behavior, drift diagnostics, and the download-before-write safety boundary.

behavior_requirements.description: Fail with the underlying diagnostic when the CBM CLI fails and no CBM session explains it.
Turn a CBM CLI call that outlives its timeout into a reported CBM error instead of stalling the apply.
Skip with an informational message and no CBM call when no native binary resolves.
Warn and exit zero when the CBM CLI fails while CBM sessions are active.
Report orphans without calling delete_project unless --apply is passed.
Keep a missing root whose parent directory is empty, as an unmounted mount point is.
Keep projects whose root is relative, empty, or absent from the listing.
Keep a missing root whose parent directory is also missing.
Never delete a root passed with --keep.
Keep a root that cannot be checked because of a permission error instead of treating it as missing.
Reject .exe and /mnt/<drive>/ CBM binaries on WSL2 so only the native Linux cache is pruned.
Require an exact task-list image match and reap the failed CLI child before probing; failed or timed-out probes cannot excuse a CLI failure.
Keep Windows drive/share roots, incompletely qualified paths, unavailable mapped or UNC parents, and case-insensitive protected roots.
Delete each orphan whose root is missing under a populated parent exactly once.
Page through every listed project before deciding what to delete.
Prefer the Windows-managed binary, fall back to native PATH, and honor an explicit override.

behavior_requirements.description: Stop Plannotator amendments and pushes after sync/config failure, missing tokens, or unexpected tracked changes; accept a no-diff result without a token.
Fail closed for terminal, malformed, unreachable, non-ancestor or octopus history, invalid-policy, and missing guarded tracking states; batch tips require their own successful CI evidence.

Select the exact linear or batch tip, or the feature parent of a single no-ff merge directly based on advertised main; preserve the pre-push contract and block guarded local-ahead rebases even with an override.
Install pinned Node and chezmoi downloads only after strict SHA-256 verification, retaining the Linux fast lane's required-capability gate.
Keep MR and standalone dependency push pipelines read-only even with a token, and stop on failed checks without staging or publishing.
Keep Renovate amendment pushes behind branch, change, and token guards with a scoped staging set and an explicit source SHA lease.
Dispatch the automatic Linux fast lane and manual platform lanes with their registered suite contracts.

Run the matching Plannotator push job against isolated Git commits, staging canonical and mirror outputs while preserving author and message and using the exact input SHA lease; register its regressions in the policy job.
Exercise the CI amendment scripts against isolated Git commits to preserve selected and legacy authors and trailers while setting the service-account committer.
Report exact-SHA outcomes, guide explicit main preparation without pushing, and accept a batch tip only after its successful evidence is prepared or reused.

entries.rationale: Offline contract suites cover job dispatch, exact-SHA status reporting, and the fail-closed feature-pipeline guard.

Offline unit and temporary-Git suites cover review-gate state transitions, transcript and SubagentHandback verdict validation, in-flight reviewer suppression and expiry, checkout isolation, path policy, legacy migration, Bash snapshot diffing with Stop-time reconciliation of background and interrupted commands, per-checkout gating of native Claude Code worktrees (including a removed worktree's hand-off to the project checkout), hook wiring, a Stop that keeps the gate when git cannot be checked, bounded Stop git budgets, and conservative wrapper fallbacks.

Reject absent, ambiguous, malformed, or substring-only Git identity matches and agent failures without replacing the last-known-good selector; report additive SSH identity conflicts without deleting existing settings.

Reject invalid lifecycle and dependency configuration with actionable diagnostics.
Reject invalid relay arguments and unsafe socket state with actionable diagnostics.
Reject malformed workspace override inputs without corrupting the active configuration.
Warn and retain existing Claude skills when the managed source is unavailable.
Reject mismatched or corrupt container Plannotator CLI and pin without publishing a false version or dropping Claude safety settings.

Stop initialization before browser-relay startup when the managed host agent helper is missing, refuses, or returns unhealthy, skipped, or malformed JSON; preserve the container key file on agent communication failure.
Open a review browser from an actual OrbStack devcontainer through the mounted descriptor and host.docker.internal without VS Code attached.
Verify Docker bind-source resolution and effective vscode UID access to the private host agent before and after host socket replacement in a separately authorized live devcontainer.
Keep live lifecycle validation inside disposable containers without exposing host secrets or config.

Atomically replace private-mode public selectors independently, preserve files on failed writes, refuse symlink, hardlink, special-file and unmanaged-fragment conflicts, and suppress raw agent identity diagnostics in isolated HOME fixtures.
Skip post-attach hooks for terminal launcher starts, and leave the VSIX cache and extensions untouched when the VS Code Server CLI is missing or unusable.
Exercise lifecycle functions without running installers or mutating host paths.
Share only the 0700 socket directory with the container, keep relay pid and log files host-side, refuse text clipboard reads, and log requests without URLs or request content.
Preserve unrelated local skills for both clients and back up conflicting Claude skill directories before linking managed content.
Qualify environment-local Claude settings migration and plugin registration with fake CLI and marketplace commands in an isolated home without touching host state.
Mount the whole WSL agent directory read-only and keep the generated container sset from launching or signaling relays or creating, removing, or changing permissions on the host socket and directory.
Install the pinned Better Beads Kanban VSIX with a usable remote Server CLI, remove conflicting extension IDs, and avoid re-downloading or re-installing after verification.

Select one exact-comment Git public identity after more than six other keys independent of order and Ansible selection; evaluate scoped GitLab/GitHub names and aliases with real offline ssh -G, preserving unrelated config and idempotent includes even when the agent is empty.
Start one private host relay per range set and relay build, open allowlisted Plannotator and rewritten Claude login URLs, and serve clipboard images to container xclip reads.

Render macOS-only read-only credential mounting, start a loopback ephemeral TCP relay, authenticate browser and clipboard operations, preserve Unix transport on WSL2, and rotate credentials after restart.
Repeat lifecycle persistence and materialization with the expected container state.
Relay concurrent bidirectional SSH-agent traffic and clean up sockets reliably.
Merge and remap workspace overrides repeatedly with stable output.
Provision all seven Unslop entrypoints and nested supporting files idempotently through Claude and OpenCode lifecycle helpers; keep Claude installation wired into create and start.
Publish an exact verified CLI pin and materialize idempotent Claude settings while preserving unrelated hooks, models, and safety permissions.

Initialize through the managed host helper with explicit matching socket variables, then start the independent browser relay; refresh the container Ansible public key through the existing agent without changing OrbStack readiness behavior.

entries.rationale: Ownership remains here until dots-7mx performs the planned same-path submodule split. Isolated suites cover lifecycle persistence and materialization, workspace override parsing and replacement, and concurrent socket relay behavior without installers or host mutation. The opt-in smoke uses a preloaded image, synthetic read-only inputs, no network, unique resources, bounded commands, and guaranteed cleanup to validate the safe production runtime phases across create, restart, and rerun. Plannotator pin publication, Claude settings migration and marketplace installation still need isolated behavioral qualification; package installers and optional network integrations remain outside the smoke boundary.

Registered standard-library tests cover session-name normalization and ref safety plus synthetic receipt parsing, formatting, mixed-case offer-code selection, CopyQ fallback, and secret-safe failures without accessing a real clipboard.
Executable mode or chezmoi naming creates a candidate signal, but these files contain data rather than automation logic.
Tests exercise production automation but are not themselves production automation targets.
Generated copies are checked against their canonical manifests and template chains rather than tested as independent implementations.

behavior_requirements.description: Reject dotted, nested, and CRLF sync.remote settings and restore only a known-safe tracked baseline without changing unrelated staged or working files.
Block guarded main rebases when local commits are absent from the policy remote tracking ref and fail closed when that tracking state is unavailable.
Fail reconciliation without claiming ownership or changing the installed legacy hook when copying fails.
Consume coauthor one-shot state before message handling, deduplicate CRLF trailers, preserve unrelated message content, and clean temporary files on success or failure.
Route push enforcement through authoritative main policy across linked worktrees, keep hooks repository-opt-in, and prevent the legacy override from authorizing GitHub pushes or guarded-main rebases.
Limit historical hook migration to exact content hashes under prepare-commit-msg; preserve edited hooks, other names, and symlinks.
Resolve local, global, and default coauthor trailers and insert the selected trailer before scissors or at the end exactly once.
Update exact historical coauthor hooks without a manifest, record ownership, and keep repeated reconciliation idempotent.
Discover, install, update, and remove owned template hooks while preserving unrelated repository hooks.
Execute-probe Python candidates for guarded hooks, reject broken command shims, fall through to a working launcher, and fail closed when none works.

entries.rationale: Contract suites cover hook ownership, synchronization, executable Beads and coauthor behavior, exact-SHA push enforcement, and guarded-main rebase protection.

behavior_requirements.description: Fail closed for invalid or conflicting policy, wrong repository/ref/SHA/workflow, superseded attempts, unavailable APIs, corrupt or stale receipts, and unsafe store ownership.

Isolate account pins without exposing tokens or switching global auth; remotely revalidate receipts; never publish from pre-push; persist before ref cleanup and prune only explicitly with fresh remote ancestry and concurrency checks.

Accept all selected successful workflow conclusions with dynamic job diagnostics, prepare feature and exact batch-main identities, and share receipts across human and agent worktrees after feature cleanup.

entries.rationale: Synthetic gh and SSH transports exercise complete merge, push-check, and evidence lifecycle behavior without provider access or installed-hook changes. GitLab Git-ref operations and topology selection retain their existing compatibility entrypoints.

The workflow runs the fast suite on GitHub-hosted ubuntu, macos, and windows runners from the GitLab push mirror as advisory evidence; it never gates a merge because no configs/pipeline-guard.json exists, so a static contract test over its triggers, matrix, pins, and artifact upload is the proportionate layer.

behavior_requirements.description: Retain collision-safe recovery state, the exact gpls stash, and any owned CI evidence ref across rebase, CI, remote-movement, cleanup, and finalization failures.
Publish only the SHA-derived reserved CI ref, lease-delete only unchanged evidence, and never push guarded main or tags.
Rebase a clean ahead-and-behind guarded main onto a pinned remote tip, obtain exact-SHA CI, restore any exact stash, and leave main ahead and ready for a separate push.

entries.rationale: Core integration tests and platform adapters cover the guarded sync state machine while agent-helper regressions preserve its shared runtime contract.
Fixture tests cover discovery, schema validation, exact-once classification, drift, candidate-list updates, and concurrent-branch merges in temporary Git repositories.

behavior_requirements.description: Skip with a warning and zero status when the CBM CLI will not start while CBM sessions hold the daemon admission gate, and fail with the underlying diagnostic when no live session explains the failure.
Warn and exit zero when no Python 3.9 interpreter is available, and propagate a nonzero pruner status.

Report INFO and exit zero when the FirefoxPWA refresh command is not deployed, warn and exit zero when it fails, and skip the runtime reinstall while web apps run or the installed Firefox is not newer.
Reject active or malformed legacy backend state, unhealthy GitHub replacements, and failed mise mutations or postconditions with nonzero ERROR diagnostics.

Reject synthetic NFS non-file inputs and failed sudo installs, stop VDI installation on a Citrix checksum mismatch, preserve CopyQ on download failure, reject invalid OpenUsage generated versions without replacing installed artifacts, and reject invalid home SSH data, symlinked targets, untrusted /usr/local directories, and sshd-rejected drop-ins before installing or by unloading the daemon and rolling the drop-in back.
Reject unsupported installed versions, PATH conflicts, command failures, and unverified Homebrew holds.
Qualify installed Claude Plannotator version and enabled-state readback against isolated fixtures; marketplace registration drift is already exercised by the host refresh tests.
Propagate selected lifecycle hook command and validation failures with actionable diagnostics.
Propagate commit-template writes, installer checksum validation, and selected lifecycle command failures without replacing valid state.
Stop macOS hydration with an actionable error when a nonempty uv manifest cannot be installed without uv.
Preserve existing fixture destinations when the redirected WSL gitignore copy, overlay render, or overlay install fails; propagate nonzero diagnostics.

Keep POSIX lifecycle hooks inside fixtures: unsupported hosts stay untouched, retirement removes only exact targets, installer writes and failure guards run against fake download, mount, signing, package-manager, and editor commands, secret-bearing hooks see only synthetic keys or fake providers, and no real credential provider is invoked. Live host integration is excluded.
Limit synthetic Sublime syntax copies, Promptfoo runtime installation, and browser policy staging to disposable homes without network or credential-provider calls.
Retire only fully qualified versions discovered under the exact UBI backend on Darwin or WSL2 while preserving unrelated installs and unsupported hosts.

Exercise selected VDI, NFS, CopyQ, LaunchAgent, OpenUsage, and home SSH branches with exact checked fixture redirects, fake network/installer/credential commands, and isolated Linux execution; reject redirect drift before execution.
Retire only the exact macOS Mnemo formula and preserve a tap still needed by another formula, without invoking Homebrew on Linux.
Limit Homebrew mutation to pinning installed OpenCode, preserve unrelated pins, and no-op without a manager or package.
Register only the pinned GitHub marketplace when absent; reject mismatched registrations and do not update after registration failure.
Keep selected cleanup, installer, optional-tool, and platform-dispatch tests inside temporary filesystems with fake network and host commands.

Require exact fail-closed fixture redirects for hard-coded WSL gitignore and devdrive targets, confine resolved paths, and assert synthetic unsupported-host no-ops without executing real host mounts or secret providers.

Leave an already-enabled cache untouched, set auto_index only when the cache reports a non-true value, reverify it afterwards, and probe for live CBM sessions with a pattern that still matches a Linux-truncated process name.
Run the CBM orphan pruner with --apply under isolated Python and protect the chezmoi working tree with --keep.
Remove all inactive legacy UBI CBM versions, reshim, verify the active GitHub replacement, and no-op idempotently when the backend is absent.

Install synthetic Zoom and local or remote Citrix payloads, converge fixture NFS settings, rate-limit CopyQ checks, retire and reload selected LaunchAgents, install or preserve matching OpenUsage artifacts, and install the home SSH drop-in, helper, and LaunchDaemon hardening-first, then converge, repair, or remove them.
Establish and reassert a stable-v1 Homebrew pin idempotently against synthetic package state.
Skip the pinned tmuxp tool at the installed version and install a mismatched version only from binary wheels without implicit Python downloads.
Register an absent Claude Plannotator marketplace at the matching tag and verify readback before continuing the refresh.
Render all lifecycle templates with synthetic Linux, macOS, Windows, and WSL2 data and parse non-empty POSIX outputs.
Render and execute selected host refresh, commit-template, cleanup, installer, and retirement hooks idempotently against synthetic state.
Copy fixture gitignore content, publish only matched synthetic overlays idempotently, configure only fixture Git, and select Debian versus non-Debian WSL cleanup.

entries.rationale: All lifecycle templates render across synthetic platform fixtures and their non-empty POSIX outputs pass shell syntax checks. Selected commit-template, cleanup, installer, pinned uv tool hydration, host-refresh, CBM auto-index reconciliation, and exact-backend CBM retirement paths have isolated behavior tests. Mnemo retirement, synthetic WSL key and Sublime syntax copies, fake Promptfoo/Mise dispatch, browser policy staging, and fake Docker image dispatch have offline behavioral tests. Selected macOS-only hooks have Linux no-op checks. Active VDI gates and synthetic Zoom/local and remote Citrix installs, NFS idempotency and rejection, CopyQ update/rate-limit, LaunchAgent retirement/reload, OpenUsage artifact checks, and home SSH install/repair/removal run with fixture-owned paths and fake commands in Linux (using a retained network-disabled container on macOS; active tests skip there without that image). WSL gitignore and overlay host-path tests fail closed on redirect drift, then execute only with disposable source/destinations and fake commands; scoped Git config and Debian/non-Debian cleanup also use fixtures. Synthetic unsupported-host no-ops and WSL-disabled package hydration are not native host-mount integration. CopyQ mount and signing failures, NFS post-install verification, VDI mount, package-discovery, and 1Password provider variants, Kanban and Plannotator install failures, Beads/Dolt link retirement scope, non-WSL package hydration, and the Claude MCP, Git-template, and host AI wrapper dispatch also execute against fakes. Hard-coded host commands and paths run only through exact-count fixture redirects. Real macOS services, mounts, installers, package managers, privileged provisioning, and production credential providers are accepted live-integration limits, not verified coverage. The planned Claude Plannotator pin readback keeps this suite partial.

behavior_requirements.description: Skip with a warning and zero status when the CBM CLI will not start, or outlives its wait budget, while CBM sessions hold the daemon admission gate, or when the installer deferred and left no binary to reconcile, and throw with the underlying diagnostic when no live session explains the failure.

Warn and skip with zero status when a coding-agent process blocks a codebase-memory-mcp download, binary replacement, or stale-process cleanup, when that process state cannot be inspected, or when the installed version cannot be read, leaving the installed binary in place for the next always-run apply to retry.
Skip with a warning without a usable Python 3.9+ interpreter, propagate helper errors, and accept successful contention skips.
Fail before launch when OpenSSH is unavailable and report fingerprint-verification and known_hosts remediation for SSH host-key failures.
Preserve timeout classification through cleanup, stop later Claude mutations after the first timeout, continue OpenCode work, and return nonzero for a later retry.

Propagate PowerShell template rendering, invalid path, and scheduled-task registration failures without writing fallback or destination state for unrelated errors; reject missing tokens and unusable WSL ports without external mutation.
Reject unsupported installed versions, PATH conflicts, command failures, and unverified Chocolatey holds in PowerShell fixtures.
Reject a mismatched Claude Plannotator marketplace tag or installed version before reporting success; qualify against an isolated Windows fixture.
Propagate selected installer, parser, and refresh failures without reporting success.
Dispatch the shared helper with isolated Python, --apply, and the protected working tree, preserving spaces and apostrophes in source and working-tree paths.
Override interactive Git SSH transport only in Claude mutation children with strict OpenSSH host-key checking and no terminal prompts, without changing caller environment.
Contain each Claude mutation, reap descendants after normal exit or timeout, fail closed before an uncontained launch, and preserve unrelated processes.
Keep broad lifecycle tests from mutating the real Windows profile, installers, or production secrets.
Verify real Windows host profile, registry, installers, and secret integration during an explicitly approved live rollout.
Limit Chocolatey fixture mutation to pinning installed OpenCode, preserve unrelated pins, and no-op without a manager or package.

Skip the Chocolatey pin write without admin rights, pass --yes on every mutation so no confirmation prompt can block an apply, emit a decodable elevated -EncodedCommand handoff, and keep the established-pin and conflicting-pin outcomes unchanged.
Qualify absent-marketplace registration, mismatched-tag rejection, and timeout containment on Windows without touching a real profile; the timeout branch still needs an isolated fixture.
Exercise PATH, profile, file-sync, cleanup, and scheduled-task behavior through temporary paths and mocked persistence or task boundaries without mutating the host.
Complete bounded Claude mutation commands with compatible output, exit status, and child-local environment behavior.
Probe python3, python, then py -3 and dispatch only a usable interpreter from the Windows-only, whitelisted pruning hook after CBM configuration.
Establish and reassert stable-v1 Chocolatey pins idempotently using a local PowerShell runtime or retained Linux audit image with mocked Windows discovery and elevation.

Register an absent pinned Plannotator marketplace and verify CLI readback before refreshing plugins on Windows; a fixture exists in tests/test_host_ai_plugin_refresh_windows.py but skips without a Windows PowerShell runtime and still needs qualification.
Render all lifecycle templates with synthetic Windows data and parse non-empty PowerShell outputs without host mutation.
Render and execute selected Windows bootstrap, file-sync, cleanup, startup-task, installer, refresh, commit-template, quota migration, and cached VSIX paths idempotently in synthetic state.

entries.rationale: All lifecycle templates render under synthetic Windows data and pass PowerShell AST parsing. Native Pester covers selected bootstrap, first-run empty PATH, profile, file-sync, cleanup, startup-task, and CBM auto-index admission and timeout behavior, while existing suites cover selected installer and refresh paths. Isolated Windows fixtures exercise the remaining hooks with temporary state, synthetic credentials, denied external commands, dry-run or no-op branches, and mocked user-scope writes; live Windows host mutation and non-dry-run installers remain untested. OpenCode pin fixtures mock Windows command discovery and elevation, and cover the unelevated -EncodedCommand handoff; native Chocolatey shim resolution, permissions, and prompting behavior remain pending under dots-6f8z for an approved rollout.

behavior_requirements.description: Turn Remote Login back off and terminate sessions when bootstrapping sshd fails or reports success without loading the service.

Turn Remote Login off for foreign or missing home signals, disagreeing samples, failed port discovery, a missing sshd hardening drop-in, and missing, malformed, non-root-owned, or group/world-writable configuration.

Rewrite every host command and the root configuration path to fixture fakes with exact counts before execution, refuse non-root callers without launchctl calls, exit on SIGTERM without changing Remote Login or sessions, never evaluate configuration values, and keep the network domain, router address, and MAC out of logs.

Enable and bootstrap sshd only when a home Ethernet link is present and every other addressed Ethernet or Wi-Fi interface is home, leave converged state unchanged, and terminate lingering SSH sessions with TERM then KILL while off.

entries.rationale: The root LaunchDaemon helper decides whether macOS Remote Login is reachable with Full Disk Access, so it is critical. Offline tests run the real helper under the system bash with fake network, launchd, and process commands; they cover the decision table, fail-closed configuration and discovery paths, idempotency, session cleanup, and log privacy. Real notifyd event delivery, TCC behavior, and launchctl on macOS remain manual on-device checks.

owner.name: managed AI adapters and destructive guards

behavior_requirements.description: Stay silent for unrelated tools, malformed input, a missing attached plan or plan path, and plan files that are missing, unreadable, or undecodable, so the ExitPlanMode guard never blocks plan approval on its own error.
Remain silent and clear transient state for failed or no-op commits and repositories without a valid feature-CI capability contract.
Reject invalid profile and project dependency state with stable nonzero diagnostics.
Reject malformed requests and state, preserve conservative provider fallback behavior, and keep permission capture failures from changing permission decisions.
Enforce destructive Beads policy when hook prerequisites parse successfully, preserve fail-open behavior when they do not, and prevent adapters from exposing or using production secrets in tests.
Deny ExitPlanMode when the attached plan differs from the plan file, and give the model a way to stop, so a plan reviewer never sees a version older than the file.
Limit post-commit adapters to local Git inspection and context injection without publication, merge, ref deletion, or implicit permission expansion.

Reject a python3 that resolves in PATH but does not run, and report a missing interpreter or hook script as a non-blocking hook error (never exit 2), so a hook guard is never skipped silently and a missing file never blocks every tool call.
Inject equivalent repository-scoped prepare-ci guidance after successful HEAD-changing wrapper commits in Claude and OpenCode.
Allow ExitPlanMode when the attached plan matches the plan file, ignoring surrounding whitespace and CRLF line endings.
Map quota, cited-search, and permission-capture requests through their supported cache, citation, and redaction contracts.
Refresh valid profiles and accept valid project dependency state through isolated adapters.

entries.rationale: Registered offline suites cover managed OpenCode compatibility, destructive Beads policy, the stale-plan ExitPlanMode guard, feature-CI reminders, profiles, and dependency guards without live credentials, network, or Beads mutations.

behavior_requirements.description: Bound malformed transcripts, pagination and sharing failures without blocking commits.
Require an observed approved Plan call, runtime model, explicit issue selection and matching worktree and branch before emitting a cross-session planner.
Recognize only literal no-ff helper invocations for the matching harness actor, rejecting unrelated commands, dynamic shells and caller-supplied handoffs.
Keep session trees and explicit payloads isolated, omit unverified source fields and persist metadata only.
Live WSL and native Windows plugin/delegate verification is manual, not automated coverage; Claude source-pair emission is explicitly deferred.
Feed runtime provenance through real POSIX and native PowerShell wrappers with exit and environment preservation.

entries.rationale: Offline fixtures exercise both producers and real wrapper commits; live harness acceptance is tracked in dots-qt9.
Shared modules are mirrored before container copies and checked against canonical bytes.

Container copies are checked against Git-tracked host sources and mirror cleanup rules. OpenCode wrapper fixtures also exercise the shared selective Go key loader with stale inheritance, rotation, credential-safe refusals, unchanged PATH and profile exports, dry-run exclusions, and dependency-guard ordering and failure propagation. These fixtures do not verify live container provisioning or provider authentication.

behavior_requirements.description: Use one aggregate execution deadline, stop owned children on cooperative cancellation, clean preparation failures, and report incomplete cleanup without masking the primary failure or retrying validation.
Refuse unknown verbs, other protocol versions, invalid slugs or SHAs, unpublished SHAs, unprepared worktrees, and non-serve commands on the forced key with exit 2.
Classify timeouts, refused connections, and authentication failures within the connect timeout, exit 3 when no peer is usable, and tell the agent to report the platform as not verified.
Run peer commands with an allowlisted environment built without a login shell so ambient secrets and client-supplied variables never reach the entrypoint.
Snapshot the working tree through a temporary index so local HEAD, index, status, and stash list are unchanged.
Reject every pushed ref outside refs/peer-env/<slug> through the per-push pre-receive hook and leave the peer's branches and HEAD untouched.
Refuse to ship untracked files whose names match secret patterns unless --tracked-only excludes them.
Refuse servers lacking the atomic lifecycle capability before publishing; retain legacy server verbs for old clients.

Accept a symlinked worktrees parent only when its resolved target is private, user-owned, and outside the checkout, git metadata, state, and registered worktrees; refuse leaf symlinks and re-pointed targets, retain ambiguous worktrees and refs, and delete a ref alone only when no worktree exists.

Confine helper writes to unique detached worktrees, peer-env refs, and private state. Remove only canonical registered owned worktrees with matching SHAs under locks, preserving busy and unrelated worktrees and ordinary branches; entrypoints run from the snapshot and are not confined.

Publish the snapshot, run cz-audit or run-tests in a unique disposable worktree, stream output, propagate remote exits and ERROR: lines, archive bounded private logs, and clean on success or failure unless explicitly retained.
Probe every other-platform peer concurrently with BatchMode and a connect timeout, cache results for the TTL, and honour --fresh and --ttl.

entries.rationale: The helper lets an agent execute on a second machine, so the ADR 0002 boundary claims (forced-command verbs only, scrubbed environment, confined refs and serve's own writes, no shell) are proven by tests that drive the real client and serve code through a fake ssh against a local clone.
Fixture tests cover authority derivation, exact divergence locks, Git-confirmed CRLF normalization, unstaged drift, byte-exact mirrors, independent section errors, and behavioral-suite exclusions.

behavior_requirements.description: Warn without inventing a gate when a before or after Git snapshot is unavailable or a hook is unpaired.
Avoid marking untouched, reverted, exempt, runtime, or oversized paths and isolate concurrent session-scoped gates.
Mark reviewable Bash changes to clean and previously dirty paths, including deletions, moves, symlinks, and executable mode.

entries.rationale: Isolated Node contract tests cover review event and state transitions, strict gate clearing, Bash dirty-snapshot success and failure paths, editor suppression lifecycle, redacted event logging, malformed inputs, and swallowed client or filesystem failures without npm or host-state dependencies.

behavior_requirements.description: Reject invalid, missing, symlinked, nested, and unowned layouts before selecting a session.
Do not attach when tmuxp fails to create the exact session or tmux cannot set its ownership marker.
Require an existing container without falling back to a host shell on failure.
Select only the unique live counterpart by pane role and reject missing, dead, or duplicate roles.
Resolve the exact session ID, reject unmarked or mismatched existing sessions, and preserve a marked session when attach fails.
Attach repeated launches without rebuilding and keep different layout sessions independent.

entries.rationale: Synthetic tmux and tmuxp fixtures exercise ownership, attach, role, and container failure contracts without contacting host services or reading private workspace data. A real tmux/tmuxp PTY test uses only test-owned sockets and synthetic layouts, and skips when POSIX PTYs or either tool are unavailable; it is not unconditional macOS runtime evidence.

platform_smoke_waiver.reason: An isolated WSL2 runner is unavailable; synthetic-home subprocesses do not validate disposable WSL2 interactive startup. At review, evaluate a throwaway WSL2 account for shell-startup-only smoke with an isolated home and disabled or stubbed credential, Windows-mount, socket, and network integrations; an account alone does not isolate provisioning.

entries.rationale: Fixture-based interactive Bash and Zsh subprocesses discover rendered startup files from synthetic homes without explicit sourcing, covering startup ordering, optional-tool absence, and synthetic environment loading; other subprocess tests cover Beads parity, modern CLI hints, PATH and WSL command resolution, package failures, and editor selection. Plannotator startup cases preserve absent, empty, and explicit remote-mode overrides from inherited or trusted-file environments on WSL2 and macOS, leave remote mode unset with synthetic SSH variables, and retain fallback and Claude port ranges. Real-repository gpls tests retain authority for guarded pull behavior. On 2026-09-28 the dedicated smoketest account ran all four native macOS interactive Bash/Zsh smoke cases without skips from the verified allowlisted bundle (fingerprint cf67f23eae2d1da12db6dfa747699ab25fd5360fd3b8d079b9af3797b94911c3, working snapshot from HEAD 12c79f944e965761420a5c2c4083ff09722c7318). That smoke is not registered with the test runner, which never passes the opt-in; it runs only through the manual procedure in docs/tooling/automation-coverage-policy.md. WSL2 interactive smoke remains unverified under a reviewable waiver and tracked under dots-4jy.10.17.

Registered offline suites cover devcontainer mirror idempotency and cleanup, sync/render sequencing, fixture-scoped secret rendering, wrapper dispatch, statusline drift, and workspace override merging and remapping. Plannotator fixtures cover successful canonical/mirror byte parity, transformed stubs, hashes, idempotency and complete Renovate pin grouping; missing/stale mirror checks and download failures; and symlink rejection, unrelated settings preservation and explicit partial-write failures. Other sync-tooling gaps remain planned.

behavior_requirements.description: Leave a v2 report with completed, interrupted, and not-run steps and an interrupted or crashed run state when a run stops early, and write a v1 report only at the end.

Retain the selected Node shim with a bounded diagnostic when mise discovery fails, times out, or returns an invalid executable, without installing, granting trust, selecting another runtime, or hiding Node execution failures as skips.
Exit 2 when the final v1 or v2 report cannot be written.

Fail a step with an explicit outcome on timeout, launch error, signal crash, Windows NTSTATUS exit, or missing required capability, and run later steps after a timeout, launch error, or missing capability.
Keep only the last 1 MiB of each step's stdout and stderr and report the omitted byte count.
Stop only the step's own PID tree on timeout and interruption from a native Windows checkout, leaving an unrelated process alive.

Stop the step's own POSIX process group, including TERM-resistant and pipe-holding descendants, on timeout and SIGINT, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP while an unrelated process survives, and kill only the step's Windows PID tree on timeout under WSL2 interop.

Give every step synthetic home, XDG, and temp directories, an empty global and system Git config, and no parent secrets; block real bd and dolt with guard shims, and sandbox directly imported tests the same way.
Match python -m unittest exit codes in the case-report adapter, record per-case outcomes and subtests in report v2, and leave report v1 unchanged.

Resolve the selected POSIX mise Node shim before replacing HOME and all four XDG roots, expose only the installed Node executable behind the command guards, and preserve runtime selection through capability probes, direct imports, and nested fixtures without passing host mise state to children.

Select suites deterministically, skip missing capabilities locally, fail them under --require-capabilities or --require-capability, reject unknown required capabilities with exit 2, keep platform mismatches as skips, and never let a guard shim satisfy bd.
Account for every concrete unittest class once per platform or as a reviewed exception, and reject class definitions the selection check cannot resolve.
Pass arguments and exit status from run-tests.sh and run-tests.ps1 through to run-tests.py.

entries.rationale: Windows owned-tree termination runs for real only under Windows Python through WSL2 interop from a \\wsl.localhost checkout; Windows interruption, NTSTATUS classification, and the taskkill fallback are exercised with mocks. Native Windows checkout behavior remains unverified, which keeps the entry partial.

Registered offline suites cover notifications, devcontainer launch actions and the workspace picker, commit and editor wrappers, WSL browser launch forwarding, host Plannotator profiles, OpenCode Go key refresh and credential-safe refusals in both host OpenCode wrappers, NFS path and lock safety, VNC preference/process transitions, Kanban pin check/write and release checksum fallback in a disposable repo with fake curl, and Promptfoo runtime dispatch and failure paths in synthetic homes. Credential fixtures do not verify live provider authentication or AoE rollout. Devcontainer rebuild fixtures cover success-only VS Code guidance, stdout and failure-status preservation, preflight refusals, process-group interruption, and nonfatal advisory-write failure; they do not exercise the VS Code UI. Maintenance tests use fake system commands and bounded fixture state. Native macOS side effects remain syntax-only rather than platform-smoked, so this broad row stays partial.

owner.name: upstream statusline and unslop backends
owner.source: upstream projects recorded by their sync workflows

entries.rationale: Local parity, version markers, entrypoints, and integrity locks cover provenance without duplicating upstream behavioral suites.
Parser and command-contract tests are offline; visible Windows banner delivery requires user confirmation.

owner.name: native Windows shell and profile automation

entries.rationale: Synthetic Windows fixtures render and AST-parse PowerShell sources. Native Pester covers profile and fragment loading, drive mapping retries, and Pageant input, process, quoting, and rerun boundaries with disposable files and mocked host integrations. Registered native-Windows cases also cover guarded gpls dispatch and commit-wrapper identity, arguments, attestation, fallback, and one-shot state. Live SMB mappings, Pageant IPC, scheduled profile startup, and other host integrations remain explicit platform-smoke gaps.

platform_smoke_waiver.reason: An isolated WSL2 runner is unavailable; fixture task failures do not validate full provisioning or host isolation.

behavior_requirements.description: Report failures from representative command-bearing Ansible tasks with actionable diagnostics.
Fail before package work without a noninteractive token and propagate package, source, and rendered Ansible dispatch failures.
Run a full provisioning smoke only in disposable WSL2 state without developer-host or secret mutation.
Exercise bootstrap and rendered provisioning dispatch with fake commands, synthetic tokens, and temporary source and config paths.
Install or skip bootstrap tools as appropriate, preserve paths with spaces, initialize the selected source, and rerun rendered Ansible dispatch with stable arguments.
Complete bootstrap and Ansible provisioning idempotently with the expected WSL2 state.
Install the pinned tmuxp wheel only when the exact uv tool version is absent and fail provisioning rather than building from source or downloading Python implicitly.

entries.rationale: Fixture tests cover bootstrap decisions, failure boundaries, quoting, rerun stability, rendered Ansible dispatch, and real isolated Ansible command-task failure diagnostics. The pinned uv tool installation gate still needs a synthetic Ansible task test on a WSL2-capable runner. Full provisioning, idempotence, and disposable WSL2 host isolation remain unverified and planned under a reviewable platform-smoke waiver.

behavior_requirements.description: Reject ssh-add communication failures even with exit code 1, and bound hung health checks, failed or incomplete Linux socket diagnostics, missing tools, lock contention, and one failed restart without retries or installation.

Identify saved-record, listener, child, and shutdown validation phases without exposing relay argument values; refuse malformed private records, unavailable lifetime evidence, and changing process identity.

Require a unique visible same-user listener with exact normalized relay arguments, grant no authority from obsolete PID metadata, reject symlinked, foreign, ambiguous, unidentified-live, or mismatching current records, and preserve other platforms, containers, agents, and healthy empty agents.
Harden only an owned legacy socket directory and identify its listener by filesystem device/inode despite duplicate pathnames from other distros or unlinked sockets.
Confirm bounded recovery against the real WSL2 socat/npiperelay/Pageant IPC chain in separately authorized isolated runtime state.
Ignore prior-boot, absent, zombie, or different-start-time record PIDs before argument validation, and recover once only after independently proving the selected listener.
Use the shared helper for shell startup, sset, and client preflight, with private records and rechecked health under a lock.

entries.rationale: Disposable sockets, real Linux socket diagnostics, synthetic cross-device responses and process records, mocked restart ownership, and rendered shell fixtures cover the helper contract without touching the developer relay. Live Windows named-pipe IPC remains unverified; the existing shell-startup WSL2 waiver is unchanged.
